title: The Palmer Table and the Lost City: a Prairie Chiropractor from Pequot Lakes to the Kalahari
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Lake Town and the Ranch

stops.name: Signau, the village the family left
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the sources give an eighteenth-century migration with no year attested; 1720 stands for the decade
stops.campa: In the Emmental, two centuries before he is born, Mennonites named Haldeman leave this village for British America under the pressure of religious persecution. He never sets foot here. The place belongs to family memory and to the surname, which is the only thing that crosses the water intact. The family moves as a household when a country turns against what it believes, and it keeps what it believes. Joshua makes the same move twice, west out of Minnesota and then south to Pretoria.
suggested_refs: Signau, canton Bern, named by Wikipedia as the Haldeman family's Swiss origin

stops.name: Pequot Lakes, the birth on the lake
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: A son is born to John Elon Haldeman and Almeda Jane Norman in a small lake town of north-central Minnesota. The father's people are Swiss Anabaptists who crossed to British America in the 1720s to escape persecution, and they have been farming somebody else's continent ever since. The father already carries the diabetes that will kill him inside the decade. The mother answers that diagnosis by going to school for a profession barely ten years old. The boy takes up her trade rather than his father's illness, and works at it for forty-eight years on two continents.
suggested_refs: Pequot Lakes, Crow Wing County, Minnesota, the birthplace; two lenses of this research gave two different wrong coordinates for it

stops.name: Minneapolis, the mother's degree
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Almeda Jane Norman Haldeman takes her Doctor of Chiropractic from E. W. Lynch's Chiropractic School, three years after the birth of her son and a year after her husband's diagnosis. The family is still in Minnesota when she graduates. Only afterwards do they cross into Saskatchewan, where she becomes, by the account that survives, the first recorded chiropractor in Canada. The profession is nine years old. She learns it to treat a man she cannot save, and she hands it forward to a boy who will carry it to Pretoria.
suggested_refs: E. W. Lynch's Chiropractic School, Minneapolis, where Almeda Haldeman qualified on 20 January 1905

stops.name: Saskatchewan, the father dies
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month, day and place unrecorded, defaulted to 1 January and to a provincial centroid
stops.campa: John Elon Haldeman dies seven years into his son's life, the diabetes having run its course in the years before insulin. The widow is a working chiropractor in a province that has never had one. She remarries a man named Heseltine Wilson; no source gives the year, and the boy passes from one household into another without the record noting the day it happens. Saskatchewan is four years old and the family is newly arrived in it. Where in the province any of this happens is nowhere written down, so the pin is the middle of it.
suggested_refs: The unrecorded Saskatchewan household of Almeda Haldeman and Heseltine Wilson

stops.name: Wilson's ranch, the boy on horseback
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the sources say only that he was reared on the ranch; neither the years nor the site is recorded
stops.campa: He is reared on his stepfather's ranch, the sources say, and they say nothing else: not which ranch, not where in a province holding a thousand of them, not for how long. He grows up in the saddle. That is the whole of the childhood record. Two decades later, when the Depression takes his own farm, he goes back to horses and rides the rodeo circuit for a living, which is a living he already knows. No source names the ranch or fixes it anywhere, so this stop is plotted at the provincial centre and stands for a place nobody wrote down.
suggested_refs: Heseltine Wilson's Saskatchewan ranch, never named or located in any reachable source

stops.name: Moose Jaw College, the first of four
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the four institutions are listed without years or sequence; this ordering is a convenience, not a record
stops.campa: He studies here, the first of four institutions the record names and none of which it dates. Moose Jaw is a railway town on the prairie and the college is a small denominational affair; what he takes from it is not written down. The same town will later supply him a wife, a dance teacher named Winnifred Fletcher, though that is twenty-two years off and neither of them knows it yet. Of the young Haldeman the record preserves a list of places attended and no degree from any of them.
suggested_refs: Moose Jaw College, Saskatchewan, first named institution in Haldeman's undated education

stops.name: Regina College, the city that keeps him
stops.date_confidence: inferred: no year attested for the attendance; the ordering is a convenience
stops.campa: The second rung of the same unsettled schooling stands in the city that will hold his entire Canadian adulthood. Within a few miles of this campus he will practise chiropractic, run the local branch of a movement the government bans, take two wives, lead a provincial party and lose three elections. He leaves Regina College without a credential, as he leaves the three other institutions the record names. The city keeps him anyway, on and off, until he is forty-seven and leaves for South Africa.
suggested_refs: Regina College, Saskatchewan, later the University of Regina

stops.name: Fort Garry, the agricultural college
stops.date_confidence: inferred: no year attested; the ordering is a convenience
stops.campa: East to Winnipeg, and to agriculture: he is training for the prairie as well as for the clinic, and for a few years after graduation he will farm. The two educations run in parallel through his twenties and the Depression will decide between them by taking the farm away. Fort Garry teaches him the science of a livelihood that dust and prices will shortly make impossible. The college sits on the Red River south of Winnipeg and is later absorbed into the University of Manitoba. No degree from here is recorded either, and he goes on to Chicago.
suggested_refs: Manitoba Agricultural College at Fort Garry, Winnipeg, absorbed into the University of Manitoba

stops.name: Chicago, the largest room he enters
stops.date_confidence: inferred: no year attested; the ordering is a convenience
stops.campa: This is the furthest his formal schooling reaches before Iowa, and the largest institution he ever enters. Chicago in the twenties runs on the proposition he will spend his life inside: that society is a machine, and that the men who understand machines ought to be running it. Technocracy Incorporated, whose Regina branch he takes over twelve years later, is built out of that proposition. He leaves the university with no named degree, as he left the three schools before it.
suggested_refs: University of Chicago, listed among Haldeman's institutions with no degree recorded

stops.name: Davenport, the Palmer degree
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unrecorded, defaulted to 1 January
stops.campa: At B. J. Palmer's school in Davenport, the institutional heart of American chiropractic, he finishes something at last. The degree is the one his mother earned in Minneapolis twenty-one years earlier, when the profession was new and she was trying to save her husband with it. He is the second chiropractor in his family and the first man in it. He carries the credential back north across the border. It feeds him for the next forty-eight years, on and off, first in Saskatchewan and then in Pretoria, where he will hold office in the national association for seventeen straight years.
suggested_refs: Palmer School of Chiropractic, Davenport, Iowa, under B. J. Palmer

segments.name: The Farm, the Rodeo, the Technocrats

stops.name: Saskatchewan, the farm lost to the Depression
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the sources give the sequence without a single date, and the farm is never named or located
stops.campa: He practises, then farms, then loses the farm to the Great Depression along with most of southern Saskatchewan. He becomes a cowboy again, and then a rodeo performer, riding for money in the years when there is no money. Afterwards he resumes chiropractic. The sequence is attested and not one date in it is. The decade leaves him certain that the economic system is broken past the reach of ordinary politics. In 1936 he takes charge of the Regina branch of a movement that proposes to abolish money and parliament together.
suggested_refs: The unnamed Saskatchewan farm lost in the Depression, and the rodeo circuit that followed it

stops.name: Regina, the first marriage
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the venue is inferred from his Regina base and is not itself attested, and the divorce is given only as 'by 1937', an upper bound
stops.campa: He marries Eve Peters, and a son, Joshua Jerry Noel Haldeman, is born the same year. The sources say the couple divorced by 1937 and say nothing further: not the day, not the ground, not what becomes of the boy. Three years of a marriage and a child's entire childhood pass inside one clause of one sentence. Where the wedding took place nobody wrote down; Regina is where he lives and works, and that is the only reason this stop stands here rather than anywhere else in the province.
suggested_refs: Eve Peters and the son Joshua Jerry Noel Haldeman, both of whom vanish from the record after 1937

stops.name: Regina, the Technocracy branch
stops.date_confidence: attested as the start of a span given as 1936-1941; month and day unrecorded
stops.campa: He leads the Regina branch of Howard Scott's Technocracy Incorporated. The movement holds that money and politicians should be abolished and that North America should be run as a single engineered energy economy by the people who understand thermodynamics. On a prairie that has just watched banks and parliaments fail together, this is not a fringe taste. He holds the position five years, and for the rest of his life he writes in its vocabulary: conspiracy and expertise, with elected government standing in the way of both. The pamphlets he prints in Pretoria twenty-four years later use the same terms.
suggested_refs: Technocracy Incorporated, Regina branch; Wikipedia's 'Technocracy movement' names Haldeman its former leader

stops.name: Vancouver, the arrest under the Defence of Canada Regulations
stops.date_confidence: attested, with a one-day discrepancy left unresolved: the 'Technocracy movement' article gives 7 October and the Haldeman article 8 October
stops.campa: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police arrest him in Vancouver under the wartime Defence of Canada Regulations. The charge is membership in an organization declared illegal: wartime Canada has banned Technocracy Incorporated outright, on the reasoning that a movement calling for the abolition of parliament is not what the country needs in the second autumn of the war. He is a chiropractor in his late thirties with a provincial party career still ahead of him, and he is now a man with a police file.
suggested_refs: The Defence of Canada Regulations and the 1940 ban on Technocracy Incorporated, lifted in 1943

stops.name: Vancouver, eight thousand dollars and a fine
stops.date_confidence: the bail, the fine and the wording are attested; the date and the venue of the conviction are not recorded anywhere reachable, and the earlier anchoring of both to Regina is unsupported
stops.campa: He is released on eight thousand dollars bail and fined two hundred dollars for writing, publishing or circulating material judged likely to cause disaffection to His Majesty. The material is a pamphlet titled Statement of Patriotism by Those Who Were Technocrats, circulated after the ban. Where he was released and where he was fined the record does not say. Nothing else survives of the proceeding except the ruling's own name for the offence, and what that phrase names is the King's feelings.
stops.quote_source: Court ruling against Haldeman for circulating the 'Statement of Patriotism,' 1940, via Wikipedia, 'Joshua N. Haldeman'
suggested_refs: The pamphlet 'Statement of Patriotism by Those Who Were Technocrats', cited in the 1940 proceeding

stops.name: Regina, the break and the newsletter
stops.date_confidence: the year of the break is attested; the newsletter's run of roughly two years is an inference, since no end year is stated in any source
stops.campa: Germany invades the Soviet Union in June and Technocracy Incorporated declares for the Soviets. Haldeman leaves. The ban that had him arrested is not what ends his involvement; the politics are. He spends the following two years attempting to build a party of his own and publishing a newsletter called Total War & Defence, and he fails at the first. The ban on Technocracy is lifted in 1943, the same year he joins somebody else's party instead. The party he tried to build leaves no name in any reachable source, and no issue of the newsletter was located in this research.
suggested_refs: Total War & Defence, Haldeman's newsletter, of which no issue was located in this research

segments.name: Social Credit and the Prairie Ballots

stops.name: Regina, the second marriage
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unrecorded, defaulted to 1 January
stops.campa: He marries Winnifred Josephine Fletcher, a dance teacher from Moose Jaw. She becomes his co-pilot and his co-author: the two of them will write a book called The Flying Haldemans: Pity the Poor Private Pilots in the middle of the next decade, by which time they will be flying light aircraft over the Kalahari looking for a city that is not there. Four children are attested from this marriage in one source and five in another. The two sources are not reconciled by either of them and are not reconciled here.
suggested_refs: The Flying Haldemans: Pity the Poor Private Pilots, by Joshua and Winnifred Haldeman, mid-1950s; no copy located

stops.name: Regina, the party and the Council
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested for both the party and the Council election; month and day unrecorded
stops.campa: He joins the Social Credit Party of Canada and, in the same year, is elected Saskatchewan's representative on the newly founded Dominion Council of Canadian Chiropractors. The two careers run together from here: the profession his mother brought into the country, and a monetary-reform party convinced that banks conspire against the producer. He will be the Council's vice president by 1947 and sit on the board of the International Chiropractors Association from 1948. The professional offices and the party work run side by side for the rest of his time in Canada, and neither interrupts the other.
suggested_refs: The Dominion Council of Canadian Chiropractors, founded in the early 1940s with Haldeman as Saskatchewan's representative

stops.name: Prince Albert, standing against the Prime Minister
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the pool gives no polling day, so the date defaults to 1 January
stops.campa: He runs for the federal parliament in Prince Albert, the riding of the sitting Prime Minister, William Lyon Mackenzie King. He places fourth with 4.3 percent of the vote. Social Credit runs candidates in ridings like this one to be counted rather than to win, and this one stands against the longest-serving prime minister the country has had. Within the year he takes the leadership of the Social Credit Party of Saskatchewan and keeps it for about five, until the year he leaves the country.
suggested_refs: The Prince Albert federal riding, held by Mackenzie King, contested by Haldeman in 1945

stops.name: Regina, the leader and the Protocols
stops.date_confidence: the speech is dated only to the 1940s in the source; 1945 places it at the start of his provincial leadership and is not itself attested
stops.campa: As leader of the Saskatchewan Social Credit party he defends his party's distribution of the Protocols of the Elders of Zion, the antisemitic forgery. His argument is not that the document is authentic. His argument is that events have been proving it out, which is an argument no evidence can reach. Fifteen years later, from Pretoria, he publishes the same reasoning at pamphlet length against a differently named enemy, and the argument is built the same way. The speech is dated only to the 1940s; the year on this stop is a placement.
stops.quote: that the plan as outlined in these protocols has been rapidly unfolding in the period of observation of this generation
stops.quote_source: Speech defending distribution of the Protocols of the Elders of Zion, quoted in Joshua Benton, 'Elon Musk's Anti-Semitic, Apartheid-Loving Grandfather,' The Atlantic, 21 September 2023, via Wikipedia, 'Joshua N. Haldeman'
suggested_refs: Joshua Benton, 'Elon Musk's Anti-Semitic, Apartheid-Loving Grandfather,' The Atlantic, 21 September 2023
sources: Joshua Benton, The Atlantic, 21 September 2023 (reached only through Wikipedia and mirrors)

stops.name: Regina, the twins
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Twin daughters, Maye and Kaye, are born to Joshua and Winnifred Haldeman. Maye will be two years old when the family leaves Canada, will grow up in Pretoria and in the back of an aeroplane over the Kalahari, will become a model and a dietitian, and will in 1970 marry Errol Musk. Nothing in the Regina of April 1948 forecasts any of that. The birth is one of the few events in this life the record dates to the day, and it is dated because of who her son turns out to be twenty-three years later.
suggested_refs: The birth of Maye and Kaye Haldeman at Regina, 19 April 1948

stops.name: Regina, the pilot's licence
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unrecorded, defaulted to 1 January
stops.campa: He earns his pilot's licence and buys a single-engine aeroplane, at forty-five, in the same year his twin daughters are born. He is a prairie chiropractor with an aircraft, which in 1948 is a thing almost nobody is. The aeroplane carries the second half of the life: the flights across southern Africa, a search for a buried city conducted from the air, thirty thousand miles to Australia and back, a book about private pilots, and a powerline outside Pretoria twenty-six years later that his wheels do not clear.
suggested_refs: Haldeman's first single-engine aircraft, bought on qualification in 1948

stops.name: Yorkton, the provincial defeat
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the pool gives no polling day, so the date defaults to 1 January
stops.campa: He contests the Yorkton constituency in the Saskatchewan general election, takes 1,792 votes and 20.26 percent, and does not win it. Saskatchewan in 1948 belongs to the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation, the first social-democratic government in North America, which is drawing the same prairie anger toward the opposite conclusion. Haldeman's answer to the Depression is conspiracy and monetary reform. His neighbours' answer is public medicine, and his neighbours have the province.
suggested_refs: Yorkton constituency returns, Saskatchewan general election of 1948

stops.name: Lake Centre, the last Canadian ballot
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the coordinate is a centroid for an abolished riding lying north and northeast of Regina, not a place, and an earlier plotting of it at Moose Jaw was wrong
stops.campa: His last Canadian campaign, in the federal riding of Lake Centre, ends with 856 votes and fourth place. The winner is John Diefenbaker, fifty-three years old, the riding's member since 1940 and eight years short of the prime ministership. Haldeman resigns as national council chairman of the Social Credit Party in the same year. Three elections in five years have returned him no seat. Within a year he is in Pretoria, explaining himself to an Afrikaner nationalist paper. The riding itself was abolished in a later redistribution, and the coordinate here is a centroid rather than a town.
suggested_refs: The Lake Centre federal riding, created 1933 from Last Mountain, Long Lake and Regina, abolished in a later redistribution

stops.name: Pretoria, the clinic near the square
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unrecorded, and the sources say only that the family emigrated, describing no manner of travel
stops.campa: The Haldemans emigrate to South Africa and settle in Pretoria, where he opens a chiropractic practice. The country has had formal apartheid for two years. His future son-in-law will say the family came because they sympathised with the Afrikaner government, and will call his father-in-law fanatical about it. Pretoria in these years is the administrative capital of a country building formal apartheid into law one statute at a time.
suggested_refs: Haldeman's Pretoria chiropractic practice, opened on arrival in 1950

stops.name: Johannesburg, the interview with Die Transvaler
stops.date_confidence: year attested; no interview date is given in any source, so the date defaults to 1 January
stops.campa: He explains himself to Die Transvaler, the Afrikaner-nationalist paper that a South African judge once called a tool of the Nazis in South Africa. The judge's phrase describes the newspaper and not Haldeman; no court ever described Haldeman at all, and the research pool that carried the phrase as a judicial finding about him was wrong. What Haldeman says about himself stands on its own. He tells the country's most extreme paper, in the year of his arrival, that the government's racial policy is not something he came in spite of.
stops.quote: Instead of the Government's attitude keeping me out of South Africa, it had precisely the opposite effect—it encouraged me to come and settle here.
stops.quote_source: Interview with Die Transvaler, quoted in Joshua Benton, The Atlantic, 21 September 2023, via Wikipedia, 'Joshua N. Haldeman'
suggested_refs: Die Transvaler, the Afrikaner-nationalist daily; the 'tool of the Nazis' description belongs to the paper, not to Haldeman
sources: Joshua Benton, The Atlantic, 21 September 2023 (reached only through Wikipedia and mirrors)

stops.name: Pretoria, the letter to the Leader-Post
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: A year after leaving Saskatchewan he writes back to the paper that covered his three campaigns, explaining apartheid to the readers of Regina. The letter runs his own route backwards, from the country he chose to the country he left. He has been in South Africa twelve months when he sets down for a prairie readership what the natives are and how they must be handled, and the Leader-Post prints it. The paper's own archive was not opened in this research; the letter survives here at second hand.
stops.quote: The natives are very primitive and must not be taken seriously... Some are quite clever in a routine job, but the best of them cannot assume responsibility and will abuse authority. The present government of South Africa knows how to handle the native question.
stops.quote_source: Regina Leader-Post, 6 August 1951, via Wikipedia, 'Joshua N. Haldeman'
suggested_refs: Regina Leader-Post, 6 August 1951; the paper's archive was not opened in this research

stops.name: Pretoria, secretary of the association
stops.date_confidence: attested as the start of a span given as 1952-1959; month and day unrecorded
stops.campa: He becomes secretary of the South African Chiropractors Association and holds the post seven years. In the same years he is flying light aircraft over oceans, driving the length of Africa in a station wagon, and walking a desert after a ruin, and through all of it he keeps the profession's minutes in Pretoria. He will be the association's president from 1959 to 1969. That is seventeen consecutive years of office in one body, held by a man who changes country, party and vehicle without much warning. The association's minutes were not reachable in this research.
suggested_refs: The South African Chiropractors Association; its minutes were not reachable in this research

stops.name: Pretoria, the disputed circuit of the world
stops.date_confidence: one source dates a round-the-world flight to 1952 and another dates a 30,000-mile flight to Australia and back to 1954; neither reconciles with the other and both are carried, as separate stops, unresolved
stops.campa: The family flies around the world in a propeller aircraft, according to the account his daughter gives; the article on Haldeman himself describes instead a flight to Australia and back two years afterwards. The two cannot be the same journey and neither source mentions the other. Both accounts agree on the aircraft and on the household aboard it. A Pretoria chiropractor is crossing oceans behind a single engine in the years when the scheduled airlines have only lately begun to cross them, and no source consulted can say in which year or on which heading.
suggested_refs: The 1952 round-the-world flight as told in Maye Musk, A Woman Makes a Plan (2019); the book was not read in this research

stops.name: Perth, the far end of thirty thousand miles
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the sources say only 'to Australia and back via Asia' and name no port of call; Perth is the most plausible landfall for a Pretoria-based flight of the period and is plotted as an approximation, not a record
stops.campa: Joshua and Winnifred fly roughly thirty thousand miles from South Africa to Australia and back by way of Asia, in a single-engine plane, with the route summarized in the sources by four words and no waypoints at all. Perth stands here for an entire continent's worth of unrecorded landings. They are amateurs doing this: a chiropractor and a dance teacher from Moose Jaw, navigating between countries in an aircraft smaller than the car they will drive across Africa two years later.
suggested_refs: The 1954 Australia flight; no Australian port of call is named in any reachable source

stops.name: Algiers, the start of the rally
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the rally's dates are not given in any reachable source
stops.campa: He enters the Algiers to Cape Town Rally in a Ford Ranch-Wagon, a family station wagon, and starts from the north coast of a continent he means to cross entire. Algeria in 1956 is two years into its war of independence and the road south runs through the Sahara. He is fifty-three, and he has been flying the Kalahari after a lost city for three years by the time he enters. The rally's own dates are not given in any reachable source. He finishes it in a wagon built to carry groceries.
suggested_refs: The Algiers to Cape Town Rally of 1956, run in a Ford Ranch-Wagon

stops.name: Cape Town, tied for first
stops.date_confidence: year attested; no finishing date is given in any reachable source
stops.campa: He crosses the line at Cape Town tied for first place, the length of Africa behind him. Above the city stands the granite memorial to Cecil Rhodes on Devil's Peak, the man who assembled the political and economic machine of the country Haldeman has driven into and chosen to live in. Margaret Murray climbed that hill in 1929 as a visiting scholar and Mark Twain lectured here in 1896 while Rhodes's premiership came apart over the Jameson Raid. Haldeman arrives as none of these. He arrives as a settler with a trophy.
suggested_refs: The Rhodes Memorial on Devil's Peak, pinned in this atlas at -33.9628, 18.4098

stops.name: Upington, the gateway on the Orange River
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1932 expedition; Haldeman's own use of Upington as a base is not attested and the stop is a reconstruction of the traditional route
stops.campa: Two decades before Haldeman's first trip, twenty-five parties under F. R. Paver and Dr. W. M. Borcherds stage from this Orange River town and go into the Kalahari after Guillermo Farini's lost city, by aeroplane and by ox-wagon, and find nothing whatever. Upington is the traditional door into that desert. Whether Haldeman used it the record does not say, and it is placed here as the door rather than as his door. The failure of 1932 is public, documented and twenty-one years old when he begins. It does not discourage him.
suggested_refs: The 1932 Paver and Borcherds expedition, staged from Upington

stops.name: The Kalahari, the first of a dozen expeditions
stops.date_confidence: attested as the start; the sources give 'beginning in 1953' and 'for over 10 years', and record no route, no camp, no site and no end year
stops.campa: He begins the search for the Lost City of the Kalahari, the ruin Guillermo Farini claimed to have seen in 1885 and that nobody has found since. There will be roughly a dozen expeditions over more than a decade, on the ground and from the air, his wife flying beside him and the children along. Back in Pretoria the family gives slide shows about them. Not one expedition route, camp or coordinate survives in any reachable source; the pin here is the middle of a desert lying across three countries.
suggested_refs: Guillermo Farini's 1885 claim of a lost city, and the aerial searches the Haldemans flew after it

stops.name: The Kalahari, the city explained away
stops.date_confidence: attested for A. J. Clement's explanation; no source records the year of the Haldemans' last expedition, and 1964 belongs to the debunking rather than to them
stops.campa: A. J. Clement accounts for Farini's ruins: they are dolerite formations, natural rock, laid down about 180 million years ago and arranged by nothing at all. The walls and the pavements were always geology. Haldeman has spent eleven years and about a dozen expeditions on them. The record does not say whether he accepted the explanation, or when he stopped going, or what he told the slide-show audiences afterwards. A man who holds that a document proves itself by unfolding is not easily argued out of a desert.
suggested_refs: A. J. Clement's 1964 identification of the 'ruins' as dolerite formations of the Drakensberg age

stops.name: Sharpeville, the massacre he is not at
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Police fire on a crowd protesting the pass laws in this township of the Transvaal. The official count at the time is sixty-nine dead; research published in 2024 argues for at least ninety-one. Haldeman is an hour's drive north in his Pretoria clinic and has no part in any of it. The massacre reaches him as material. Within weeks he converts the killings into evidence that the apartheid state is the party under attack, and pays a printer to put it in circulation.
suggested_refs: The Sharpeville massacre, 21 March 1960, in the Transvaal province of the day

stops.name: Pretoria, the pamphlet after the massacre
stops.date_confidence: the sources place the pamphlet 'weeks after' Sharpeville and give no publication date; April 1960 is a placement, and dating it to 21 March, as an earlier lens did, imports the date of the massacre itself
stops.campa: He self-publishes The International Conspiracy to Establish a World Dictatorship and the Menace to South Africa. The argument is the Regina argument about the Protocols, moved south and recast: a coordinated global power is dismantling white Christian civilization, and South Africa is its last redoubt. He is fifty-seven, president of his professional association, and paying out of pocket to print this. The pamphlet has never been digitized, and every line of it quoted anywhere descends from one magazine article written in 2023.
stops.quote: the white man's integrity, initiative and independence make him the most difficult to control
stops.quote_source: Joshua Haldeman, The International Conspiracy to Establish a World Dictatorship (self-published pamphlet, 1960), via Wikipedia, 'Joshua N. Haldeman'
suggested_refs: The International Conspiracy to Establish a World Dictatorship and the Menace to South Africa; no copy located in this research
sources: Joshua Benton, The Atlantic, 21 September 2023 (reached only through Wikipedia and mirrors)

stops.name: Pretoria, the argument about the majority
stops.date_confidence: the same undated pamphlet as the preceding stop, separated here only to carry a second passage; the date is a placement and carries no evidential weight
stops.campa: The same pamphlet sets out what the conspiracy wants from Africans: their use as an instrument against the settler. The people around him in Pretoria appear in his prose as a lever somebody else is pulling. The word primitive is the word he sent to Regina in 1951. He has been in the country ten years; his clinic, his aircraft, his association and his desert expeditions all run on the labour and the land of a state constructed to keep those people out of the vote, and the pamphlet's grievance is that the state is under attack.
stops.quote: oust the white man, who has in a few years brought their people from primitive savagery to a great measure of peace and security

stops.name: Pretoria, the conspiracy in health
stops.date_confidence: the pamphlet is undated in every reachable source; the early 1960s placement follows the quotes lens and is not a record
stops.campa: In a second self-published tract, The International Conspiracy in Health, he attacks water fluoridation, vaccination and health insurance as instruments of control. In the same pages he grants the state full authority over Black South Africans, on the parental model. Compulsion is tyranny when it reaches him and guardianship when it reaches them, and the tract does not notice the difference. It carries no date anywhere in the reachable record and is known, like everything else he printed, only through quotation.
stops.quote: The State has the right to do for them what it thinks is best, the same rights as the parents have for their children

stops.name: Pretoria, president of the association
stops.date_confidence: attested as the start of a span given as 1959-1969; month and day unrecorded
stops.campa: He becomes president of the South African Chiropractors Association and holds it ten years, the decade in which he writes both pamphlets. The professional standing and the conspiracy tracts belong to the same man in the same city in the same years, and nothing in the record suggests his colleagues found the combination remarkable. He signs both as a respected officer of his profession, not as a fringe figure operating outside it.
suggested_refs: The presidency of the South African Chiropractors Association, 1959-1969

stops.name: Pretoria, the daughter marries
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unrecorded, defaulted to 1 January
stops.campa: Maye Haldeman marries Errol Musk. She is twenty-two and has spent her childhood in the back of her father's aeroplane over a desert with no city in it. Her husband will one day tell journalists what his father-in-law believed: fanatical about apartheid, sympathetic to the Nazis. Most of what is known about Joshua Haldeman's politics reaches the record through that son-in-law, fifty years late and by way of this wedding. He has four years to live and does not know what the marriage will eventually publish about him.
suggested_refs: Errol Musk's characterization of his father-in-law, quoted in the 2023 press

stops.name: Pretoria, the grandson
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Elon Musk is born in Pretoria, the son of Haldeman's daughter Maye. Joshua Haldeman is sixty-eight and has two and a half years left; he will die before the boy turns three. The grandson will remember nothing of him directly. What reaches the boy instead is his grandmother's stories of the flights and the expeditions across two continents, and an inherited appetite he will later describe simply as a desire for adventure, exploration, doing crazy things.

stops.name: Wonderboom, the powerline
stops.date_confidence: the date and the manner of death are attested; the airfield is not named in any reachable source, and Wonderboom, Pretoria's principal light-aircraft field, is plotted as an approximation
stops.campa: Practising landings near Pretoria, he catches a powerline with his wheels. He and a passenger are killed. He is seventy-one. The kind of aircraft that carried him to Australia, over the Kalahari, and around whatever circuit it was in 1952 kills him in the pattern above a home field. Which field nobody wrote down. The pin here is Wonderboom, the principal light-aircraft aerodrome at Pretoria, and it is a guess offered as one: no reachable source names the site of the crash or the passenger who died with him.
suggested_refs: Wonderboom aerodrome, Pretoria, plotted as an approximation for an unnamed crash site

stops.name: Pretoria, no grave and one rereading
stops.date_confidence: the article's date is attested; the wider revival is a general press consensus from roughly 2023 onward and is not tied to any single verified source
stops.campa: No burial site, no marker, no plaque, no exhibit: nothing was found in any reachable record, in Canada or in South Africa, of where he was put or whether anything stands over him. For half a century he is a footnote in the history of chiropractic. Then journalists go looking for the ancestry of his grandson, and what comes up out of the ground is the pamphlets rather than the man. The Atlantic prints the Protocols speech and the Leader-Post letter in September 2023. That is the whole of his afterlife.
suggested_refs: Joshua Benton, 'Elon Musk's Anti-Semitic, Apartheid-Loving Grandfather,' The Atlantic, 21 September 2023
